title: Euler's Seven Bridges of Königsberg and the Birth of Graph Theory (1736)
explainer: Graph theory traces its origin to a 1736 paper by Leonhard Euler, who resolved a puzzle about whether a walker could cross all seven bridges of Königsberg exactly once by stripping away everything except the connections between landmasses. Euler showed such a walk is possible only when at most two landmasses have an odd number of bridges, introducing the idea of representing a problem as nodes and edges, the same abstraction every graph algorithm in this lesson relies on.

title: Independent Discovery of Minimum Spanning Tree Algorithms
explainer: The greedy minimum-spanning-tree idea was discovered independently at least three times: by Otakar Borůvka in Czechoslovakia in 1926 to help plan an electrical grid, by Vojtěch Jarník in 1930 (a method later rediscovered by Robert Prim in 1957), and by Joseph Kruskal in 1956. That several different greedy strategies, developed decades apart by people unaware of each other's work, all provably produce an optimal spanning tree is a concrete illustration of why greedy algorithms need real correctness proofs rather than just intuition.
